faq.question: How to convert JSON to CSV for Excel?
faq.answer: Paste your JSON array, click Convert to CSV, and download the file. The converter automatically adds a UTF-8 BOM so Excel on Windows correctly recognizes the encoding. For older Excel versions or Chinese locale, you can select GBK encoding.

faq.question: Does it support nested JSON objects?

faq.question: Can I select which fields to export?

faq.question: How to preview the CSV before downloading?
faq.answer: After converting, a table preview appears automatically. You can also toggle it using the 'Show Table Preview' button. This helps you verify column names and row content before downloading.

faq.answer: The converter collects all unique keys from all objects in the array and uses them as CSV column headers. If a particular object does not have a certain key, the corresponding cell in that row will be empty.

faq.question: Is my data uploaded to a server?

article.title: How to Convert JSON to CSV for Excel & Google Sheets
article.content:
Why Convert JSON to CSV?

JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is widely used for data exchange between servers, APIs, and applications. However, when you need to analyze this data, create reports, or share it with non-technical team members, CSV (Comma-Separated Values) is often the preferred format. CSV files can be opened directly in Excel, Google Sheets, and most spreadsheet applications.

Common Use Cases

  • API data export: Convert API responses (JSON) to CSV for analysis in Excel or Google Sheets
  • Database backups: Export database records stored as JSON to a spreadsheet-friendly format
  • Data migration: Move data between systems that use different formats by converting via CSV
  • Reporting: Create charts, pivot tables, and summaries from JSON data in a spreadsheet
  • Manual review: Turn structured JSON into a human-readable table for QA, auditing, or content review

Handling Nested JSON Objects

Real-world JSON data is often nested. For example:

{"user": {"name": "Alice", "address": {"city": "NYC"}}, "status": "active"}

When flattening is enabled, the converter turns this into CSV columns such as:

  • user.name → Alice
  • user.address.city → NYC
  • status → active

This dot-notation style keeps the structure clear while remaining compatible with flat CSV tables.

How to Convert JSON to CSV

  1. Paste JSON array: Add a JSON array of objects to the input field. Each object will become one row in the CSV.
  2. Configure options: Enable 'Flatten nested objects' if your data contains nested structures. Choose UTF-8 or GBK encoding depending on your Excel version and locale.
  3. Click Convert: The tool parses the JSON, collects all unique keys, and generates a CSV representation.
  4. Preview and select fields: Use the table preview to check column names and row content. Optionally select only the fields you want to export.
  5. Download CSV: Save the result as a .csv file and open it in Excel, Google Sheets, or another spreadsheet application.

Excel Compatibility Tips

  • Use UTF-8 BOM: The converter adds a Byte Order Mark (BOM) to the CSV so Excel on Windows correctly recognizes UTF-8 characters.
  • GBK encoding: For older Excel versions or Chinese locale environments, select GBK encoding if you see garbled characters.
  • Field selection: Export only the fields you need to keep your spreadsheet clean and focused.
  • Check delimiters: Most systems expect comma-separated CSV. If your locale uses semicolons, you may need to adjust Excel's import settings.

Best Practices

  • Preview first: Always check the table preview before downloading to ensure columns and rows look correct.
  • Validate input: Make sure your JSON is a valid array of objects. Inconsistent structures may lead to many empty cells.
  • Flatten wisely: Use nested flattening when you need inner fields, but be aware that deeply nested data can create many columns.
  • Large files: For very large JSON files (for example, 100MB+), consider splitting them into smaller chunks before conversion.
  • Keep a backup: Retain the original JSON in case you need to re-export with different options or fields.

Client-Side Privacy

This JSON to CSV converter processes input in your browser instead of requiring an upload to a remote service. That can be convenient for internal datasets, sensitive reports, or development data. However, you should still avoid entering passwords, API keys, access tokens, or other highly sensitive information into any browser-based tool.

article.title: 如何将 JSON 转换为 Excel 和 Google Sheets 可用的 CSV
article.content:
为什么要将 JSON 转换为 CSV？

JSON（JavaScript 对象表示法）广泛用于服务器、API 和应用程序之间的数据交换。然而，当你需要分析这些数据、创建报表或与非技术人员共享时，CSV（逗号分隔值）往往是更合适的格式。CSV 文件可以直接在 Excel、Google Sheets 和大多数电子表格应用中打开。

常见使用场景

  • API 数据导出：将 API 响应（JSON）转换为 CSV，方便在 Excel 或 Google 表格中分析
  • 数据库备份：将以 JSON 格式存储的数据库记录导出为电子表格友好的格式
  • 数据迁移：在不同格式的系统之间迁移数据时，通过 CSV 作为中间格式
  • 报表生成：在电子表格中基于 JSON 数据创建图表、数据透视表和汇总
  • 人工审核：将结构化 JSON 转换为人类可读的表格，用于 QA、审计或内容检查

处理嵌套 JSON 对象

现实世界中的 JSON 数据通常是嵌套的。例如：

{"user": {"name": "Alice", "address": {"city": "NYC"}}, "status": "active"}

启用展平后，转换器会将其转换为如下 CSV 列：

  • user.name → Alice
  • user.address.city → NYC
  • status → active

这种点号表示法在保持结构清晰的同时，也能与扁平的 CSV 表格兼容。

如何将 JSON 转换为 CSV

  1. 粘贴 JSON 数组：在输入框中添加一个 JSON 对象数组。每个对象会变成 CSV 中的一行。
  2. 配置选项：如果数据包含嵌套结构，可以启用“展平嵌套对象”。根据 Excel 版本和使用环境选择 UTF-8 或 GBK 编码。
  3. 点击转换：工具会解析 JSON，收集所有唯一键，并生成对应的 CSV 表示。
  4. 预览并选择字段：使用表格预览检查列名和行内容，必要时只选择要导出的字段。
  5. 下载 CSV：将结果保存为 .csv 文件，然后在 Excel、Google Sheets 或其他电子表格应用中打开。

Excel 兼容性技巧

  • 使用 UTF-8 BOM：转换器会在 CSV 文件开头添加字节顺序标记（BOM），使 Windows 版 Excel 正确识别 UTF-8 字符。
  • GBK 编码：对于旧版 Excel 或中文环境，如果在 Excel 中看到乱码，可以尝试切换到 GBK 编码。
  • 字段选择：只导出需要的字段，可以让电子表格更简洁、重点更突出。
  • 检查分隔符：大多数系统使用逗号分隔的 CSV。如果你的区域设置使用分号，可能需要在 Excel 导入设置中调整分隔符选项。

最佳实践

  • 先预览：下载前务必检查表格预览，确认列和行符合预期。
  • 验证输入：确保 JSON 是有效的对象数组。结构差异过大会导致大量空单元格。
  • 合理使用展平：在需要内部字段时启用嵌套展平，但要注意过深的嵌套会产生很多列。
  • 大文件处理：对于非常大的 JSON 文件（例如 100MB 以上），可以考虑先分块再转换。
  • 保留备份：保留原始 JSON 文件，以便之后用不同选项或字段重新导出。

浏览器本地处理与隐私

这个 JSON 转 CSV 转换器在浏览器中处理输入内容，不要求将数据上传到远程服务。对于内部数据集、敏感报表或开发数据来说，本地处理更加方便。不过，仍然不建议在任何浏览器工具中输入密码、API 密钥、访问令牌或其他高度敏感的信息。
